content:
devon_support: FYI customer Acme (private deployment in us-west-2) started getting 503s and "connection reset" for API calls after a maintenance window. They report peering dropped and BGP went down. Root log excerpt below.

lisa_network: @devon_support can you paste the ipsec logs and BGP adjacency state? Any recent cert rotation?

devon_support: They rotated certs overnight (customer-side). Attaching snippets: 
```
Mar 12 03:14:22 ipsec[1]: IKEv2: SA established with 198.51.100.12
Mar 12 03:15:01 ipsec[1]: IKEv2: Child SA rekey failed: CERT_VERIFY_FAILED: CRL fetch timeout
```
Also BGP: `Neighbor 10.0.0.254 Admin down (received notification)`

raj_ops: CERT_VERIFY_FAILED + CRL fetch timeout screams egress block to OCSP/CRL. Check firewall egress allowlist for our CA endpoints and ocsp responders. Also check UDP NAT-T (4500) and UDP 500 connectivity plus MTU. Run on the tunnel endpoint: `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'udp port 500 or udp port 4500 or tcp port 80 or tcp port 443'` and share a 15s capture.

elaine_infra: We also saw BGP route flap on the DX VIF earlier — repeated IPsec tear downs will cause route withdraws and transient route suppression. Root cause chain likely: OCSP/CRL blocked -> cert validation fails during rekey -> IPsec tears child SA -> BGP adjacency drops. Recommended quick fixes: allow outbound 80/443 to ocsp.acme-ca.example and crl.acme-ca.example, open UDP 500/4500 to peer IP 198.51.100.12, set tunnel MTU to 1420, and increase DPD/keepalive (e.g., `dpdaction=restart dpddelay=10`).

samir_sre: Repro steps I used in lab:
1) Blocked outbound to OCSP with a firewall deny -> saw `CERT_VERIFY_FAILED` in ipsec logs -> IKE rekey fails repeatedly.
2) As child SA dropped, BGP adjacency timed out and went Admin Down.
3) Allowing OCSP/responder restored IKE and then BGP.

Config snippet from customer (sanitized):
```
conn redwood-acme
  keyexchange=ikev2
  ike=aes256-sha256-modp2048
  esp=aes128gcm16
  left=%any
  leftid=@acme-vpn
  right=198.51.100.12
  rightid=@redwood-gw
  dpdaction=restart
  dpddelay=30
```

sre-bot: ALERT: peering-degraded acme-usw2 detected at 2026-03-17T03:20:00Z — auto-ticket #INC-20260317-912

lisa_network: Also check whether the customer has OCSP stapling enabled. If the peer disables stapling and the firewall blocks OCSP, the cert chain verification will fail on rekey. Stapling mitigates the need for outbound OCSP in some cases.

devon_support: Customer updated firewall to allow OCSP endpoints + CRL (80/443) and opened UDP 500/4500 to 198.51.100.12, set MTU to 1420 on the tunnel interface, and restarted the IPsec service. Post-change status: IPsec SAs re-established and BGP adjacency returned. They observed a handful of 503s while caches and in-flight requests recovered. Customer confirmed full recovery at 03:46 UTC.

elaine_infra: Ops follow-ups we should add to runbook: 1) Add egress allowlist examples for OCSP/CRL/responder URLs & IP ranges in Private deployment onboarding. 2) Validate OCSP reachability as part of cert rotation playbook. 3) Document MTU guidance and recommend 1420 for DX/VPN hybrid setups. 4) Add a small health-check that verifies IKE child SA creation after certificate changes.

devon_support: Thanks team — I'll update the customer with root cause (egress block prevented OCSP/CRL fetch which caused cert verification to fail -> IPsec rekeys failed -> BGP withdrew routes -> API 503s). Closing once the customer ack arrives. :white_check_mark:
